brief.headline: Ask for a 10–15% price cut: they keep 7.4% profit versus 5.0% for similar firms, so there's room in the price they charge you

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.basis: They keep 7.4% profit versus 5.0% for similar firms — that extra margin is room to give back. Market research shows ₹0.55–1.20/pc for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (cut from 30 to 15 days) in exchange for 3–4% off the price
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster costs us ₹1.64 L in cash tied up, but they borrow money at 7.02%, so getting cash 15 days sooner is worth roughly 3.5% annualized to them — trade that for a permanent price cut

brief.financialLeverage: PGP Glass is very healthy — they made ₹3373.51 Cr in sales, keep 7.4% profit (better than the 5.0% their peers keep), and carry a CARE A+ / Stable credit rating. Their cash is stuck for 78 days versus 71 for similar firms, so they're slightly tighter on cash than average. But we're tiny — just ₹39.99 L or 0.01% of their revenue — so on our own we have almost no pull. The play: bundle this with other packaging spend, dangle a multi-year deal, and openly qualify a second source (Manjushree or Mold-Tek) to show you're serious about switching if they won't move.

evidence.point: They keep more profit than peers
Strong credit rating — no supply risk
Their cash is stuck slightly longer than similar firms

evidence.figure: ₹39.99 L spend, 0.01% of their ₹3373.51 Cr revenue

evidence.point: Market asking price for 28 mm PP caps

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, does pharma bottles and caps, health score B (65/100) — a very strong second source

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader at ₹946.50 Cr, serves pharma with pails and containers, health score B (73/100) — credible alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed blow-moulded packaging player at ₹701.17 Cr, broad capability across bottles and caps, health score C (51/100)

risks: We're 0.01% of their sales — bundling more volume or a longer contract is the only way to get their attention
They have EPF payment delays and pending legal cases flagged — watch for any supply hiccups, though the A+ rating suggests these are minor
Their financial health sits in the 'grey' zone (Altman Z 1.45) — not distress, but not bulletproof. If you push too hard and they walk, lining up Manjushree or Mold-Tek will take time
Market backup leads (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are unqualified — verify and price them before using as leverage
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in a three-year deal at a lower price — you're keeping 7.4% profit versus 5.0% for the market, and we're seeing ₹0.65–0.80 quotes elsewhere for similar caps, so let's find a number that works for both of us.
